claim: Opening turn emphasizes positioning over aggression; map awareness through scouts and fighters yields mutual information parity.
Balanced unit deployment (scouts, armor, infantry, bomber, launcher) across opening prevents overcommitment and maintains defensive flexibility.
Aggressive early scout clashing yields map control but risks unit losses before positioning is secure.
Concentrating strikes on wounded units across multiple turns achieves attrition advantage, especially mid-game.
Strike drone kamikaze without interceptor support exposes it to direct counter-strikes and wastes potential.
Losing visibility through early unit destruction forces defensive consolidation, enabling opponent to control tempo.
Committing air units without mutual fighter cover against radar-equipped defenses leads to rapid losses.
Early bomber activation without sufficient armor support enables enemy air-to-ground concentration that breaks offensive cohesion.
Maintaining mutual overwatch between armor and infantry in late game reduces attrition and preserves unit count for final consolidation.
Coordinated multi-unit strikes against isolated targets eliminate threats faster than distributed attacks.
Early scout advantage allows sustained pressure; superior vision lets you dictate engagement timing.
Concentrating fire on wounded units guarantees kills; splitting strikes on healthy targets wastes damage output.
Air units without ground support are picked off; fighter + bomber without cover become priority kills.
